page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is an entry-level virtual instance within the ecs.e family built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via a KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile comprises 8 virtual CPUs allocated on a shared basis across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores operating at 2.5 GHz with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration features 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU core. It provides no bundled local NVMe or SSD storage and relies entirely on remote block storage, while network connectivity operates at a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate moderate multi-threaded capacity balanced by limited single-thread throughput. Multi-core operations score in the middle tier, evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 11,140.77, a multi-core stress-ng result of 7,072.24, static web serving throughput of 10.17 GB/sec, and Redis SET performance of 9.25 million operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics fall in the lower percentile ranges, with a Geekbench single-core score of 859.0 and reduced throughput in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests.

The shared vCPU architecture offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for budget-sensitive deployments requiring multi-threaded capacity without sustained peak performance. The chief operational tradeoff involves potential vCPU resource contention and weak single-core execution speed. Consequently, the instance is appropriate for lightweight web serving, microservices, software testing and compilation, and general-purpose background task processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is a shared-CPU virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.e family, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor under the x86_64 architecture with a KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero bundled local storage. Benchmarks place overall multi-core performance, Passmark CPU scores, and Redis SET throughput in the average tier, though single-core compute, text processing, and compression routines show lower relative efficiency due to shared vCPU scheduling. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio delivers economical resource density for cost-sensitive operational tiers. Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is well-suited for lightweight web application hosting, software compilation, development environments, microservices, and modest database workloads.
